title: God washes and cleanses: Ezekiel, Titus, Ephesians, 1 Cor, Psalm 51
source_text: XI. Ideoque quum Deus tollit ex nobis peccati malitiam dicitur nos abluere, purgare, & mundare. Et huc spectat illa Dei promissio apud Ezechielem, Effundam super vos aquam mundam, & mundabimini ab omnibus inquinamentis vestris, Ezech. 36. Et quod dicit Paulus ad Titum, Christum dedisse semetipsum pro nobis, ut nos mundaret sibi populum acceptabilem, sectatorem bonorum operum. Tit. 2. Quibus consonat quod scribit ad Ephesios, nempe, Christum seipsum tradidisse pro Ecclesia, ut eam sanctificaret, mundans eam lavacro aquae per verbum. Eph. 5. Eaque ratione mundati & abluti erant Corinthii, quibus dicit idem Paulus, Haec quidem fuistis, sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis, in nomine Domini Jesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri. 1 Cor. 6. Atque hanc spiritualem lotionem petebat David, Psal. 51. Asperges me Domine hyssopo, & mundabor; lavabis me, & supra nivem dealbabor.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore when God takes away from us the malice of sin he is said to wash, purge, and cleanse us. And hither looks that promise of God in Ezekiel: I will pour clean water upon you, and you shall be cleansed from all your filthinesses (Ezekiel 36). And what Paul says to Titus, that Christ gave himself for us, that he might cleanse for himself an acceptable people, zealous of good works (Titus 2). With which agrees what he writes to the Ephesians, namely that Christ gave himself for the Church, that he might sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing of water through the word (Ephesians 5). And in that way the Corinthians had been cleansed and washed, to whom the same Paul says: Such indeed you were, but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God (1 Corinthians 6). And David sought this spiritual washing (Psalm 51): You will sprinkle me, Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be clean; you will wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
pass_b_english: Taking away sin's malice means washing and cleansing (Ezekiel 36; Titus 2; Ephesians 5).
Corinthians were washed, sanctified, justified (1 Corinthians 6); David begged hyssop-washing (Psalm 51).
